chunks: Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Miskān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled that the mudabbar is from the one-third, and that a man may revoke his bequest, adding to it or reducing from it, so long as he has not died.

key_terms.الثُّلُثِ: The one-third portion of the estate available for bequests.
key_terms.الْمُدَبَّرَ: A slave promised freedom upon the master's death.
key_terms.يَنْقُضَ وَصِيَّتَهُ: To revoke or undo his bequest.

ai.seo_question: Can a person change or revoke his bequest before death, and is a mudabbar counted from one-third of the estate?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on bequests and a mudabbar slave, stating that the mudabbar is counted from the one-third of the estate. It also establishes that a person may alter, increase, decrease, or revoke his will during his lifetime, so long as death has not occurred.
